text: Rent is a refundable deposit, not a fee. Minimum account balance = (128 + data size in bytes) x lamports_per_byte; the 128 bytes are fixed storage overhead. Closing an account returns the deposit. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Solana rent is a one-time, fully refundable minimum-balance deposit, not a recurring fee. An account must hold (128 + data_len) x lamports_per_byte lamports. The 128 is fixed storage overhead. Closing the account returns the whole deposit to the destination the closer names. Rent exemption is no longer time-based: SIMD-0194 (Activated) renamed lamports_per_byte_year to lamports_per_byte and fixed exemption_threshold at 1.0. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Rent minimums should be read from the getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption RPC (or the Rent sysvar), never hardcoded, because the rate changes with each SIMD-0437 step. Local solana-test-validator 4.3.0 still starts at 6,960 lamports per byte, so reclaim logic should be tested on Devnet. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Raydium says it added admin instructions to return rent held by its pool vaults and state accounts: AMM v4 WithdrawExcessLamports (tag 18) and CPMM and LaunchLab CollectExcessLamports on 2026-09-09, and CLMM CollectExcessLamports on 2026-09-30. Stable AMM has none. The sweep moves lamports only, so token balances and swap quotes are unchanged, and a CLMM position's own rent still returns only when the position is closed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Two safeguards cover a rent increase. The SIMD-0438 reset gate (set_lamports_per_byte_to_6960) can raise the rate back to 6,960 for new allocations. SIMD-0392 (Activated; Chainstack gives mainnet slot 443,664,000) changes the post-execution floor to min(rent minimum, pre-execution balance) when an account has a balance, does not grow and keeps its owner. An account that already withdrew its excess therefore stays usable after a reset, unless it grows, changes owner or loses lamports below its starting balance. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Reclaiming early forfeits nothing: each later step over-funds the account again, and the excess has no deadline. The only cost of reclaiming is the base fee per transaction. Sweeping after each step collects the excess as it appears; waiting for step 5 collects it in one pass. Raydium adds that a frozen token account still qualifies, because freezing restricts token movement, not lamports. (medium confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Revival attack: if a program zeroes an account's lamports but a later instruction in the same transaction refunds rent-exempt lamports, the account survives the runtime's end-of-transaction cleanup. Solana's program-security course documents this risk, and RareSkills notes that reassigning ownership to the System Program defuses it. (low confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: The classic Token and p-token instruction lists contain no mint-close instruction: CloseAccount covers token accounts, and AuthorityType has no mint-close variant (inferred from the absence in the instruction list). A classic mint's deposit therefore cannot be refunded by closing. The mint authority can still sweep the excess above the minimum with WithdrawExcessLamports. If the authority is revoked and the mint account cannot sign, nothing can sweep it; Raydium says LaunchLab's base mint is stranded this way by design. (medium confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Reclaim sweep recipe: list the wallet's token accounts under both the Token and Token-2022 programs, skip native (wrapped SOL) accounts, compute excess = lamports minus getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption(space) (cache one lookup per distinct size), then send WithdrawExcessLamports in batches of 20 per transaction, each instruction addressed to the program that owns its source. Simulate first. Raydium measured 270 compute units per instruction on Token and 1,414 on Token-2022. The 20-per-transaction figure comes from the 1,232-byte transaction limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-07)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Revival attack: the runtime deletes a zero-lamport account only after the transaction completes. An attacker can invoke a close and add a transfer in the same transaction that refunds the rent-exempt lamports, so the account survives and the program may act on stale data. The Solana course advises zeroing the data and tagging a closed discriminator; RareSkills describes the same risk and the same attack path. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Scanner services flag two rent-reclaim lookalikes as drainers. MalwareTips rates solclaimer.app High Risk (44/100). Its verdict rests on two PhishDestroy reports, a 207-day-old domain and no business records; antivirus engines and blocklists were clean, and the site is listed on Phantom and DappRadar. PhishDestroy first recorded refundsolana.net on 2026-03-18 with a critical 100/100 score, 8 of 94 VirusTotal engines flagging it and a Spamhaus DBL phishing listing, under the headline 'Get Your SOL Back Instantly | Recover Rent from Solana Token Accounts'. The two scanners are not independent for solclaimer.app. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: A platform that sponsors rent can lose it when users close accounts: the refund goes to the destination the closing signer names, not back to the sponsor. Turnkey writes that refunded lamports 'may go to the signer, not back to you'. Its mitigations: reuse a constrained set of token accounts instead of create-and-close loops; strip SPL Token CloseAccount instructions (discriminator 9) before submission; set Jupiter wrapAndUnwrapSol to false and manage wSOL explicitly; apply spend caps, rate limits and alerts. Filtering is weaker if users can export or control the signer key. (medium confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: The rent reduction moves no lamports. Existing accounts keep their old, higher balances; the gap between balance and the new minimum is 'excess' that the owner can withdraw. For a 165-byte token account the excess is 183,711 lamports after step 1 and 1,835,352 lamports at step 5; a 182-byte Token-2022 account holds 194,370 excess at step 1. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Token and Token-2022 token accounts, mints and multisigs can return excess rent without being closed via the WithdrawExcessLamports instruction (discriminator 38). The account stays open, keeps its token balance and drops to the current minimum. Required signer: the token account owner, the mint authority, or the multisig signers; a mint with no mint authority needs the mint account itself to sign. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Excess rent has no deadline: it stays in the account, and reclaiming early does not block a later sweep. Each later step over-funds the account again, so the reclaimable excess grows from step to step. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Closing an SPL token account (CloseAccount) deletes it and returns its full rent deposit to a destination account chosen by the owner or close authority. For ordinary token accounts the token balance must be zero first (burn or transfer out). Wrapped SOL accounts are the exception: closing them with a balance recovers both the rent and the underlying SOL. (low confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Rollback safeguards exist: SIMD-0437 depends on SIMD-0392 (relaxed post-execution min-balance check) so rent can be raised back to 6,960 if state grows too fast; SIMD-0438 can reset the rate, and SIMD-0389 does so automatically. Per Chainstack, accounts whose balance was reduced stay valid after a reset only if they do not grow, change owner, or fall below their starting balance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: WithdrawExcessLamports also rescues SOL that someone sent directly to a Token-Program-owned account, which could not be moved before. The Solana docs call this SOL 'previously stranded', and the interface comment describes the instruction as a way to rescue SOL sent to any token-program-owned account while leaving only the rent-exempt lamports. (medium confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: The rate cut moves no lamports. An account funded before a step keeps its balance. The gap between that balance and the new minimum is excess that only the account's authority can withdraw (for a program-owned account, only the owning program). Nothing is refunded automatically and no deadline applies; the excess stays in the account until withdrawn. AMBCrypto concludes the change resembles capital recovery, not an airdrop. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Excess per account = (128 + data_len) x (old rate - new rate). A 165-byte token account funded at 6,960 holds 183,711 excess lamports after step 1, 550,840 after step 2 and 1,835,352 after step 5. A 182-byte Token-2022 account holds 194,370 excess after step 1. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Only the program that owns an account can debit it, so excess rent on a program-owned account (PDA) stays until that program ships a reclaim instruction. A safe instruction verifies the account's owner and the authority's signature, reads the floor from Rent::get() at call time, moves only the excess, and credits exactly what it debits. System Program wallets have no separate excess to reclaim. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Revival attack: a program that closes an account by zeroing its lamports does not delete it until the transaction ends. An attacker adds a transfer in the same transaction that refunds the rent, and the account survives. Safe closing moves the lamports, reassigns the owner to the System Program and shrinks the data. Current Anchor close() does this: it credits the destination, sets lamports to 0, calls assign(system_program::ID) and resize(0), and rejects closing an account into itself. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: A local solana-test-validator 4.3.0 starts at 6,960 lamports per byte even with --clone-feature-set, so a reclaim script finds no excess locally. Test on Devnet, where steps 1-2 are active as on mainnet. A test harness with an older bundled SPL Token build lacks instruction discriminators 38 and 45, so the sweep fails on an unknown discriminator. Test against a mainnet-cloned token program. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-07)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Client support: getWithdrawExcessLamportsInstruction is exported by @solana-program/token (the Token program), and the Token-2022 program exposes the same instruction through @solana-program/token-2022. Docs use @solana/kit. Pass { programAddress: account.owner } so each instruction goes to the program that owns its source. For a multisig authority, pass the co-signers with multiSigners. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: A rate cut moves no lamports. An account created before a step keeps its balance, so it holds an excess of (128 + data length) x (old rate - new rate). A 165-byte token account holds 183,711 excess lamports after step 1, 550,840 after step 2 and 1,835,352 after step 5. A 182-byte Token-2022 account holds 194,370 after step 1. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: SIMD-0392 (Activated; authors Igor Durovic and Jon C of Anza) lets an existing account stay below the current rent-exempt minimum if its pre-execution balance is above zero, its size does not grow and its owner does not change. The floor is then min(current minimum, pre-execution balance). Growth or an owner change requires the current minimum. Chainstack dates its mainnet activation at slot 443,664,000. This grandfathering makes a later rate increase non-disruptive. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: SPL Token CloseAccount deletes a token account and sends all its lamports (rent plus any extra) to a destination chosen by the owner or the close authority, who signs. It fails with InvalidAccountData if source and destination are the same account, and with NonNativeHasBalance if a non-native account still holds tokens. A frozen account with a zero balance can still close. The account that paid to create an associated token account gets nothing back automatically. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: Only the owning program can debit a program-owned account, so excess rent on a program's PDAs needs an instruction in that program. The Foundation's checklist: verify the account is owned by the program, verify the authority signer, read the floor from the Rent sysvar, move only the excess, and conserve lamports across the transaction. Programs you do not control often have no such instruction. (high confidence)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: A local solana-test-validator 4.3.0 starts at 6,960 lamports per byte even with --clone-feature-set, so a reclaim script finds no excess there; test on Devnet, where steps 1-2 are active. A local build with an older bundled SPL Token program fails a sweep on an unknown discriminator. On a wrapped SOL account WithdrawExcessLamports fails with 'Instruction does not support native tokens'; on a mint with no authority it fails with 'Account does not support specified authority type' unless the mint signs. A second run reports 0 reclaimable until the next step activates. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-07)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds

text: A rent sponsor that pre-funds accounts can lose the deposit. Turnkey's rent sponsorship (an Enterprise-plan feature, off by default) pre-funds the signer for new accounts, and the refund goes to the close destination, usually the signer or owner, not the sponsor. Turnkey's mitigations: strip CloseAccount (discriminator 9) before submission, set Jupiter's wrapAndUnwrapSol to false and manage wrapped SOL explicitly, reuse a constrained set of token accounts, and apply deny policies, spend caps and monitoring. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
keywords: Rent and token account closure refunds
